issues.t: Airbag control module can short out (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on. In rare cases an airbag or seat belt pretensioner could fire without a crash, or the airbags might not work in one.
issues.why: The airbag control module (SRS ECU) can develop an internal short circuit. Toyota recalled 2004-2006 xA models in 2018.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A Toyota dealer will inspect the module and replace it free if needed.

issues.sym: The A/C cuts in and out, blows warm, or the compressor makes noise. Some owners report the compressor clutch staying engaged or the shaft breaking.
issues.why: Owners of 2005-2006 xAs in particular report a pattern of failed compressors, sometimes just after the warranty ended. Failed internal electronics and the magnetic clutch have been blamed.
issues.next: Have the system diagnosed before just recharging it. If the compressor has failed, ask a shop to check for debris in the system, and ask Toyota about goodwill help on low-mileage cars.

issues.sym: The A/C works but never gets really cold, even on the coldest setting.
issues.why: The temperature control cable can be out of adjustment, so the blend door lets some heat through.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check and adjust the temperature control cable before replacing any A/C parts.

issues.t: Check engine light from VVT-i oil control valve or cam gear
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with stuttering acceleration or a rough idle.
issues.why: The variable valve timing (VVT-i) system fails: the oil control valve or the camshaft timing gear wears or sticks. This is the most-reported xA problem on RepairPal, at about 115,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Fresh oil at the right level matters for this system. A shop can test the oil control valve before replacing the cam gear.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant level dropping.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and starts leaking, often between 50,000 and 140,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the pump replaced before the engine overheats. Replacing the drive belts at the same time saves labor.

issues.sym: A squeal on start-up or with the A/C on, or belts that crack or wear quickly.
issues.why: The xA has no automatic belt tensioner, so the belts must be tensioned by hand and can loosen soon after being replaced.
issues.next: Ask the shop to set the belt tension correctly and recheck it after a few weeks.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP system leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative emissions code. The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: Leaks at the charcoal canister, filler neck or a vacuum switching valve, or water in the evaporative system, trigger the light. Toyota issued a bulletin about water in the system.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks shut first. If the light returns, have a smoke test done to find the leak.

issues.t: Check engine light for lean codes P0171 or P2195
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a lean code or an oxygen sensor code. You may notice hesitation.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for these codes on the xA. Causes include sensor issues and air or fuel delivery problems.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check the bulletin. Have intake leaks and the airflow sensor checked as well.

issues.t: Clogged fuel injectors causing rough running
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation or misfires, and lower fuel economy.
issues.why: Deposits clog the fuel injectors. Toyota issued a bulletin with a cleaning procedure.
issues.next: An injector cleaning service is usually the first step; replace an injector only if it still fails tests.

issues.sym: Stuttering, shaking at idle, and a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: An individual ignition coil fails.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. Replace the coil and check the spark plugs.

issues.sym: A whine or growl from the gearbox that changes with speed, getting louder over time.
issues.why: A mainshaft bearing inside the manual transmission wears out, reported around 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the transmission checked early. A bearing failure left too long can damage gears, turning a rebuild into a replacement.

issues.t: Engine won't crank because of a bad clutch switch
issues.sym: On manual cars, the engine sometimes doesn't crank when you turn the key with the clutch pressed.
issues.why: The clutch pedal safety switch fails, so the starter never gets the signal. One owner replaced a starter before finding this.
issues.next: Ask the shop to test the clutch switch before replacing the starter or battery.

issues.sym: A loud hum or growl that rises with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: A wheel bearing wears out, typically past 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the bearing replaced. A badly worn bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble.

issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattling underneath, or exhaust smell.
issues.why: Exhaust pipes, hangers and the muffler rust out and leak.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Leaks near the cabin can let fumes in.

issues.t: Airbag light from failed clock spring
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on; the horn or wheel buttons may also stop working.
issues.why: The clock spring, a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel, breaks.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The driver airbag may not work while the light is on.

issues.sym: One door won't lock or unlock with the power locks.
issues.why: The lock actuator motor inside the door fails.
issues.next: Use the key in the meantime. The actuator inside the door is a fairly simple part to replace.

issues.sym: Squealing or grinding when braking.
issues.why: Worn front pads and rotors are the usual cause. Some cars squeal because of missing or worn anti-noise shims, which Toyota supplied free to at least one owner.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected soon. Grinding usually means the pads are worn to metal and are damaging the rotors.

issues.t: Creak or tick at the top of the windshield
issues.sym: A creak, tick or rattle near the top of the windshield over bumps.
issues.why: Two small stoppers bonded to the windshield can rub against the body and make the noise. Toyota issued a bulletin with a fix.
issues.next: It's harmless but annoying. Ask a Toyota dealer or glass shop to look at the bulletin repair.

issues.sym: The car drifts or pulls to one side on a straight road.
issues.why: Uneven tire pressures, tire construction or wheel alignment are the usual causes. Toyota issued a bulletin on diagnosing pulling.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures first, then try swapping the front tires side to side. If it still pulls, have the alignment checked.

issues.t: Accessory cruise control may not return to idle (recall)
issues.sym: After switching cruise control off, the engine doesn't drop back to idle.
issues.why: Certain Rostra cruise control units installed by distributors or sold as accessories can fail to release the throttle.
issues.next: Most xAs never had cruise control from the factory. If yours has an add-on unit, check the recall status with a Toyota dealer or Rostra, and press the brake to cancel cruise until it is fixed.
